title: Book: One Up on Wall Street — Peter Lynch (1989)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: Fund manager Peter Lynch argues that ordinary investors can find good companies in places they already know, such as the products and services they use at work and in daily life, before professionals notice them. He sorts stocks into rough types — slow growers, stalwarts, fast growers, cyclicals, turnarounds and asset plays — and stresses understanding why you own a stock, checking the business basics and valuation, and holding while the story is intact. Cautions: it takes time, research and temperament; knowing a product is not enough to know the stock is cheap; most people do better with diversified index funds; and the book is a US classic from a very strong market period. This is an educational summary, not a recommendation to pick stocks.
